# Rotterdam depot

Rotterdam is a chilled-goods depot open 06:00 to 22:00, and the only site with the larger cold room. It runs three shifts, each led by a shift lead with six pickers [src: doc:docs/depots.md; doc:docs/staff.md].

## Cold room

The cold room holds 40 pallets at 2 to 8 °C [src: doc:docs/depots.md]. If the room passes 8 °C for ten minutes, the shift lead moves the pallets to the backup room and calls facilities on extension 4410; the alarm is logged in the incident book within the hour [src: doc:docs/alarms.md]. See [cold-chain alarm response](../procedures/cold-chain-alarm.md). Insulated gloves are required for cold-room work lasting more than ten minutes [src: doc:docs/safety.md].

## Freight and returns

Nordfreight carries chilled goods between Rotterdam and [Hamburg depot](hamburg-depot.md) on Tuesdays and Fridays, and must present a temperature log at hand-over [src: doc:docs/carriers.md]. Returns are inspected at the depot that shipped them, and chilled returns must arrive within 24 hours of dispatch or are destroyed [src: doc:docs/returns.md]. See [returns handling](../procedures/returns-handling.md).

# Rotterdam depot

Rotterdam is a chilled-goods depot open 06:00 to 22:00, and the site with the network's largest cold room. It runs three shifts, each with a shift lead and six pickers [src: doc:docs/depots.md; doc:docs/staff.md].

## Cold room

The cold room holds 40 pallets at 2 to 8 °C [src: doc:docs/depots.md]. If it passes 8 °C for ten minutes, the shift lead moves the pallets to the backup room and calls facilities on extension 4410, and the alarm is logged in the incident book within the hour [src: doc:docs/alarms.md]. Insulated gloves are required for cold-room work lasting more than ten minutes [src: doc:docs/safety.md]. See [cold-chain alarm response](../procedures/cold-chain-alarm.md).

## Freight and returns

Nordfreight carries chilled goods between Rotterdam and the [Hamburg depot](hamburg-depot.md) on Tuesdays and Fridays, presenting a temperature log at hand-over [src: doc:docs/carriers.md]. Returns are inspected at the depot that shipped them, so chilled goods dispatched from Rotterdam come back to Rotterdam; chilled returns must arrive within 24 hours of dispatch or are destroyed [src: doc:docs/returns.md]. See [returns handling](../procedures/returns-handling.md).
", "path": "wiki/entities/rotterdam-depot.md"}

# Antwerp depot

Antwerp opens at 07:00, the latest opening of the depots, and has no cold room at all [src: doc:docs/depots.md]. Chilled goods therefore depend on the refrigerated rooms at [Rotterdam depot](rotterdam-depot.md) and [Hamburg depot](hamburg-depot.md) rather than Antwerp [src: doc:docs/depots.md].

## Shifts

The site runs two shifts, fewer than Rotterdam's three [src: doc:docs/staff.md]. The documents do not state Antwerp's closing time or its pallet capacity (unverified). No cold-chain alarm rule is recorded for Antwerp, which is consistent with its lack of a cold room [src: doc:docs/alarms.md].
", "path": "wiki/entities/antwerp-depot.md"}

# Hamburg depot

Hamburg opens at 05:30, the earliest of the depots, and runs a cold room of 25 pallets [src: doc:docs/depots.md]. Its night shift is staffed differently from the other sites: a night manager rather than a shift lead [src: doc:docs/staff.md].

## Cold chain

A cold-room alarm at Hamburg pages the night manager, instead of the phone escalation used at [Rotterdam depot](rotterdam-depot.md), and the alarm is entered in the incident book within the hour [src: doc:docs/alarms.md]. See [cold-chain alarm response](../procedures/cold-chain-alarm.md). Cold-room work beyond ten minutes requires insulated gloves [src: doc:docs/safety.md].

## Lanes and drills

Baltic Reefer carries chilled goods from Hamburg to the [Gdansk depot](gdansk-depot.md) on Mondays, and Nordfreight runs chilled goods between Hamburg and Rotterdam on Tuesdays and Fridays; each carrier presents a temperature log at hand-over [src: doc:docs/carriers.md]. The last quarterly fire drill at Hamburg found a blocked exit, since cleared [src: doc:docs/safety.md].
", "path": "wiki/entities/hamburg-depot.md"}

# Prague depot

Prague's cold room holds 30 pallets at 2 to 8 °C, between Rotterdam's 40 and Hamburg's 25 [src: doc:docs/depots.md]. The depot closes at 21:00, earlier than the 22:00 closing recorded for the rest of the network [src: doc:docs/depots.md].

## What is not recorded

The documents give no opening time, shift pattern or carrier lane for Prague, and no cold-chain alarm rule for it, although refrigerated storage in the 2 to 8 °C band is what the alarm procedure protects elsewhere [src: doc:docs/depots.md; doc:docs/staff.md; doc:docs/alarms.md; doc:docs/carriers.md]. Chilled goods returning to Prague must arrive within 24 hours of dispatch or are destroyed, since returns are inspected at the depot that shipped them [src: doc:docs/returns.md]. See [returns handling](../procedures/returns-handling.md).

# Gdansk depot

Gdansk is the newest depot, opened in 2025, and handles dry goods only [src: doc:docs/depots.md]. It has no recorded cold room, consistent with its dry-goods scope [src: doc:docs/depots.md].

## Chilled arrivals

Despite that scope, Baltic Reefer carries chilled goods from the [Hamburg depot](hamburg-depot.md) to Gdansk on Mondays, presenting a temperature log at hand-over [src: doc:docs/carriers.md]. The documents do not say where those chilled goods are stored once in Gdansk, nor Gdansk's opening hours or shift pattern (unverified) [src: doc:docs/depots.md; doc:docs/staff.md]. Dry goods are accepted as returns for 30 days at the depot that shipped them [src: doc:docs/returns.md].
", "path": "wiki/entities/gdansk-depot.md"}
